chapter: Joining Earl Hines and the Grand Terrace
title: Why the band succeeded: radio and Hines's unpredictable piano
summary: Radio carried the band; Hines never played anything the same way twice.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: What do you think the reason is for the success of the Earl Hines band? In those days. The radio broadcasts, or --
Well, Hines himself was an outstanding instrumentalist. Did people really dig his playing, or --
I mean, they understood what he was doing?
Now, he sometimes can play -- still does, in fact, but back then play some pretty wild things.
Were they pretty much the same way all the time, or --
No, all together different. That's where my ear really came in handy.
Boy, it was a mess working with him, because he never played the something the same way.
Did you have any problem keeping up with him, or --
No, didn't have a bit of problem.
How'd the band get along with each other and with Earl?
Oh, fine. We got along fine.
